unlock.first_20_boundary: Improves the first salvage decision after bathy-drop survival by naming which emergency crate contents create repair choices.

metadata.truth_payload: The emergency float crate is a limited survival budget, not a loot box.
metadata.player_question: Which crate item should become shelter, power or signal confidence first?

en_US.title: Emergency Float Crate Inventory
en_US.scanner: FLOAT CRATE // Buoyant seal intact. Repair stock limited. Open near shelter route.
en_US.terminal: DROP SUPPORT INVENTORY // Foam charge low; battery slab stable; mirror packed; stock label salt-damaged.
en_US.audio: Do not empty the crate just because it opens. Make the first repair count.
en_US.in_game_wiki: The emergency float crate is a limited survival budget. Use repair stock for pressure, first power and signal confidence before stripping comfort items.
en_US.external_site: The emergency float crate is the first argument against panic. It contains enough to make one or two good decisions, not enough to erase the crash. A battery slab can wake a dead panel. Emergency foam can buy air time. The crate teaches scarcity before the inventory screen does.
en_US.field_note: A full pocket and a leaking wall is still a bad trade.

unlock.first_20_boundary: Turns crash debris into a visible trail, insulation source and route-reading lesson.

metadata.truth_payload: Loose heat-shield teeth are route markers and salvage stock; intact shelter plating should not be stripped.
metadata.player_question: Which debris is safe stock, and which debris still protects the shelter?

en_US.title: Heat Shield Teeth Salvage Trail
en_US.scanner: HEAT-SHIELD TOOTH // Ablative ceramic. Good insulation, sharp edge, useful trail marker.
en_US.terminal: DROP MATERIAL NOTE // Loose ceramic teeth mark descent shear. Do not strip pressure shell plating until shelter integrity is known.
en_US.audio: White teeth in the reef mean the drop came apart this way. Follow the bite marks.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Heat-shield teeth are loose ablative ceramic from the descent burn. They mark the crash path and provide insulation stock if the player does not strip shelter-critical plating.
en_US.external_site: Heat-shield teeth are ugly, useful and honest. They show where the bathy-drop bled speed into water and reef. The pieces are good insulation, sharp enough to punish careless hands and bright enough to make a trail through storm churn.
en_US.field_note: Loose teeth are stock. Teeth still holding your wall together are not.

unlock.first_20_boundary: Explains why Black Keel exists but cannot receive a clean rescue packet until repair and sky timing align.

metadata.truth_payload: Carrier contact is physically blocked by damage and route noise, not by narrative convenience.
metadata.player_question: What repair chain makes one useful Black Keel packet possible?

en_US.title: Broken Uplink Core Fracture
en_US.scanner: UPLINK CORE // Antenna bus fractured. Packet integrity below recovery threshold.
en_US.terminal: DROP DIAGNOSTIC // Uplink core fracture detected; ascent package missing; carrier handshake partial; recovery threshold not met.
en_US.audio: Black Keel heard a broken shape. Make it hear a sentence.
en_US.in_game_wiki: The broken uplink core can form fragments, not recovery-grade packets. Repair contact path, power and relay support before spending a clean orbital window.
en_US.external_site: The broken uplink core is the first reason the sky cannot simply solve the game. Black Keel is above HECTON-8, but the drop's antenna bus is cracked, the contact seat is salted and packet integrity never reaches recovery threshold.
en_US.field_note: A reply that cannot carry coordinates is weather with a voice.

unlock.first_20_boundary: Makes the shallow service buoy a repairable signal object and not environmental dressing.

metadata.truth_payload: Old infrastructure can pass weak pings after cleaning, grounding and alignment; it cannot create rescue by itself.
metadata.player_question: What makes this buoy support one useful carrier packet?

en_US.title: Shallow Service Buoy Salted Receiver
en_US.scanner: SERVICE BUOY // Receiver salted. Ground strap damaged. Weak ping possible after cleaning.
en_US.terminal: SERVICE BAND // Receiver confidence degraded by salt ingress. Mast offset exceeds clean-window tolerance.
en_US.audio: The buoy is not dead. It is dirty, bent and tired. Fix those in order.
en_US.in_game_wiki: A salted shallow service buoy can boost weak carrier contact after cleaning, grounding and mast alignment. It cannot turn a bad orbital window into rescue.
en_US.external_site: The shallow service buoy is old Deep Reach infrastructure doing one small job badly. Clean the contact, ground the line, wait for the window, then ask the sky for less than a miracle.
en_US.field_note: Old infrastructure lies less than new contracts. It just fails louder.

unlock.first_20_boundary: Makes the first beautiful ecology useful as oxygen cue, bait and route signal without making the shallows horror-only.

metadata.truth_payload: Shallow life helps the player before it scares them; intact ecology is more useful than dead stock.
metadata.player_question: What does this beautiful organism tell the player about air, bait and current?

en_US.title: Halo Sargassum Oxygen Lure
en_US.scanner: HALO SARGASSUM // Oxygen bubbles trapped in mat edge. Useful cue; avoid stripping whole patch.
en_US.terminal: ECOLOGY NOTE // No terminal surface. Scanner and PDA route only until a future authored ecology table admits this packet.
en_US.audio: Bright mat, bubbles on the lip. Good air nearby. Do not tear up the sign.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Halo sargassum marks oxygen-rich shallow water and small-fauna traffic. Harvest lightly; intact mats remain better route cues than dead stock.
en_US.external_site: Halo sargassum is a first kindness with teeth. The mat catches light, traps oxygen bubbles and attracts small life to its edge. A player can use it for emergency air cues, bait and current reading, but ripping it out blindly turns a useful patch into a rotten slick.
en_US.field_note: The first pretty thing that saves you is still a thing you can ruin.
